# Chemical Burn First-Aid Checklist

## Before You Begin
- [ ] Ensure your own safety — wear gloves or protect your hands before touching the victim
- [ ] Move the victim away from the chemical source if safe to do so
- [ ] Identify the chemical if possible (check container labels, ask the victim or bystanders)
- [ ] Call emergency services (911 or local number) or confirm someone else has

## Immediate Treatment

### Step 1: Remove Contaminants
- [ ] Remove the victim's clothing, jewelry, and accessories near the burn area (chemicals can soak into fabric)
- [ ] Cut clothing off rather than pulling it over the burn if necessary
- [ ] Brush off any dry chemical powder before applying water (if instructed by the product label)

### Step 2: Flush the Burn
- [ ] Rinse the affected area with cool, running water for **at least 20 minutes**
- [ ] Keep water flowing away from unaffected areas — avoid spreading the chemical
- [ ] Do NOT use hot water, ice, or very high-pressure streams
- [ ] For eye burns: hold eyelids open and flush continuously from the inner corner outward

### Step 3: Protect the Wound
- [ ] After flushing, loosely cover the burn with a clean, dry cloth or sterile non-stick dressing
- [ ] Do NOT apply ointments, creams, butter, or neutralizing agents (e.g., vinegar or baking soda)
- [ ] Do NOT break any blisters

## Monitor the Victim
- [ ] Watch for signs of shock: pale skin, dizziness, shallow breathing, fainting
- [ ] Keep the victim warm and comfortable (avoid overheating the burn)
- [ ] Keep the victim calm and still
- [ ] If the victim becomes unresponsive but is breathing, place them in the recovery position
- [ ] Be prepared to perform CPR if breathing stops

## While Waiting for Paramedics
- [ ] Continue flushing if pain persists or the chemical is still suspected on skin
- [ ] Note the chemical name/type and how long contact occurred — give this to paramedics
- [ ] Keep the chemical container or Safety Data Sheet (SDS) available if possible
- [ ] Record the time the burn occurred and when flushing began
- [ ] Do not give the victim food or drink

## Warning Signs Requiring Urgent Attention
- Burns to the eyes, face, mouth, or genitals
- Difficulty breathing
- Chemicals that penetrate skin (e.g., hydrofluoric acid)
- Signs of severe reaction: confusion, vomiting, rapid deterioration

---
*This checklist is a general guide. Always follow specific instructions from emergency dispatch and product safety labels when available.*
